headline: From engineering education to projects, promotion and collective support
summary: Black engineering careers include institution-building, technical qualifications, workplace training and student organizing. These examples concern particular disciplines; they do not make every engineering job the same path.
coverageNote: Four episodes involving Howard, Iowa, NASA Langley and Purdue. Civil and aerospace engineering records are not automatically evidence for every specialty or engineering manager.
question: Which hiring, project assignment, qualification or promotion record connects Black engineers to your workplace?

events.title: Howard's trustees authorize engineering degree programs
events.people: Howard's trustees, faculty and engineering students
events.decisionMaker: Howard University's Board of Trustees approved the programs in 1907.
events.barrier: The college identifies educating Black engineers as its institutional mission; this source does not describe each student's admissions barriers.
events.change: Civil, electrical and mechanical engineering entered the curriculum over the following years.
events.outcome: By 1911 Howard had established a four-year bachelor's curriculum and an equipped school building.
events.limit: Program creation establishes education, not an employer's hiring practices or every graduate's placement.

source.title: Howard University College of Engineering and Architecture · Our History
source.locator: 1907 trustees' approval; 1907–1910 curriculum and 1911 four-year program paragraphs

events.title: Archibald Alexander moves from a degree into engineering work and ownership
events.people: Archibald A. Alexander, George F. Higbee and Maurice A. Repass
events.decisionMaker: Iowa awarded Alexander's degree; Marsh Engineering employed him; Alexander later founded his own firm.
events.barrier: Iowa identifies him as its first Black civil-engineering graduate.
events.change: After graduating in 1912, Alexander joined Marsh Engineering and established his own company in 1914.
events.outcome: His later firm built projects including Iowa's power plant and tunnels and the Moton Airfield used by Tuskegee Airmen.
events.limit: This documents his employment and business projects, not an industry-wide end to exclusion.

source.title: University of Iowa College of Engineering · Archibald A. Alexander
source.locator: Biography: 1912 graduation, Marsh Engineering employment and Alexander & Repass projects

events.title: Mary Jackson gets permission to train and earns an engineering promotion
events.people: Mary W. Jackson and engineer Kazimierz Czarnecki
events.decisionMaker: The City of Hampton permitted her attendance; Langley promoted her after she completed the required courses.
events.barrier: Graduate-level classes needed for the training program met at segregated Hampton High School.
events.change: With Czarnecki's encouragement, Jackson requested access, attended the classes and completed the training.
events.outcome: NASA records her 1958 promotion and subsequent research on supersonic aerodynamic effects.
events.limit: A documented promotion at Langley does not prove equal access to engineering advancement at other employers.

source.title: NASA · Mary W. Jackson
source.locator: Biography: Supersonic Pressure Tunnel, permission for Hampton classes and 1958 engineering promotion

events.title: Black engineering students turn local support into a national organization
events.people: Edward Barnette Jr., Fred Cooper, Arthur Bond and Purdue's Chicago Six
events.decisionMaker: Student organizers and their faculty adviser formed the local group; participating students established NSBE nationally.
events.barrier: The organizers addressed Black engineering students' recruitment, retention and professional representation.
events.change: The Purdue group invited students from other campuses to build a national organization.
events.outcome: NSBE reports that 134 students from 28 schools gathered at Purdue on April 10–12, 1975.
events.limit: The meeting and organization are documented; the source does not isolate their effect on a particular student's graduation or job.

source.title: National Society of Black Engineers · Convention media kit
